metaTitle: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): A Guide for India
metaDescription: What generative engine optimization (GEO) is, how AI answers pick sources, GEO vs SEO vs AEO, a 10-step checklist and how to measure AI visibility.
title: Generative engine optimization (GEO): what it is and how to do it in India
excerpt: A plain-English GEO guide for Indian businesses: how ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and Perplexity choose sources, how GEO differs from SEO and AEO, a 10-step checklist and how to measure it.
intro: Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the work of making your business easy for AI answer systems such as Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Copilot to find, understand, trust and cite. In practice it is SEO applied to AI answers: indexable pages, clear answers to real buyer questions, evidence other sites confirm, and separate measurement of AI visibility.

This guide explains where the term comes from, how AI answers choose their sources, what changes compared with ordinary SEO, and a 10-step checklist an Indian business can follow. Nobody can guarantee a citation in an AI answer, and this guide does not pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: What is generative engine optimization?
paragraphs: The term "generative engine optimization" comes from a 2023 research paper by Pranjal Aggarwal and co-authors, later presented at the KDD 2024 conference. The researchers tested how changes to a page's content affected how often it was used in answers produced by a generative search system.

Since then the market has filled with overlapping labels: GEO, AEO (answer engine optimization), AI SEO, LLM SEO and AIO. They describe roughly the same goal. Google's own 2026 guide to its generative AI features mentions AEO and GEO as terms people use and treats the work as part of SEO. Microsoft Bing uses the phrase generative engine optimization in its webmaster guidelines and says SEO fundamentals support eligibility for AI-generated experiences.

So the useful definition for a business is simple: GEO is the part of your organic growth work that decides whether AI answers mention you, describe you correctly and link to you when a buyer asks a question you should be the answer to.

sections.heading: How AI answers choose which websites to cite
paragraphs: Most AI search answers are not written from the model's memory alone. Google describes two techniques behind AI Overviews and AI Mode. Retrieval-augmented generation (also called grounding) retrieves relevant, current pages from the search index and builds the answer from them, with links to those pages. Query fan-out sends several related searches at once, so a question like "best way to get more website traffic" may also fetch results for "technical SEO checklist" or "why is my website not ranking".
ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Copilot work in a broadly similar way: they search, read a handful of pages and summarise them. That has three practical consequences.
list: If a page is not indexed or crawlable, it cannot be retrieved, however good it is. Google says a page must be indexed and eligible to show a snippet to appear in its generative AI features.
Pages that already rank well for the fan-out searches have a better chance of being read. Ordinary rankings still matter.
The answer is assembled from passages. A page that states a clear, specific, well-supported answer is easier to use than one that buries it under introduction and sales copy.

sections.heading: GEO vs SEO vs AEO: what is actually different
paragraphs: The three overlap far more than vendors suggest. The differences are mainly in the result you are aiming for and how you measure it.

after: Read the [AEO guide](/blog/answer-engine-optimization-aeo) for the answer-writing side in more depth. If someone sells GEO as a replacement for SEO, ask what they will do that is not SEO. Usually the honest answer is measurement and entity work, which are worth paying for, but they sit on top of a healthy site, not instead of one.

sections.heading: What does not help (and what Google says you can ignore)
paragraphs: A lot of GEO advice online is untested. Google's guide for its AI features lists several things site owners do not need to do for Google Search. Other engines publish less, so treat their behaviour as uncertain rather than assuming the opposite.
list: Special AI files or markup. Google says it does not use llms.txt or other AI text files for Search. An llms.txt file is harmless and some tools read it, but it is not a ranking or citation switch.
Chopping content into tiny chunks. Google says its systems understand pages with several topics and there is no ideal length.
Rewriting everything "for AI". Write for the buyer; AI systems understand synonyms.
Buying or faking mentions. Inauthentic mentions are not as helpful as they look, and spam systems are designed to discount them.
Treating structured data as a GEO trick. Schema is not required for AI features. Keep it accurate because it helps rich results and clarity, not because it guarantees a citation.

sections.heading: The 10-step GEO checklist for an Indian business
paragraphs: Work through these in order. The first four are foundations; skipping them makes the rest pointless.
list: Check indexing. In Search Console, confirm your key service and guide pages are indexed. Fix "Discovered – currently not indexed" pages with internal links from your strongest pages before writing anything new.
Serve the real content in HTML. If your copy only appears after JavaScript runs, some AI crawlers may never see it. Prerendered or server-rendered pages remove that doubt.
Decide your crawler policy deliberately. OpenAI documents OAI-SearchBot (search) separately from GPTBot (training). Blocking training does not have to mean blocking search visibility.

Write one canonical description of your business. Same name, one-line description, location, services and founder on your homepage, About page, Organization schema, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn and directory listings. AI answers repeat what the web agrees on.

List the 20–30 questions buyers actually ask. Use Search Console queries, sales calls, WhatsApp enquiries and People Also Ask. Include unbranded questions such as "best SEO agency for D2C brands in India".
Give each question one owner page. Answer it in the first 40–70 words under the heading, then explain conditions, costs, steps and exceptions.

Add information only you have. Google calls this non-commodity content: first-hand process, real numbers with definitions, photos of real work, named people with real credentials. Summaries of other blogs are easy to replace.

Earn mentions on sites AI answers already trust. Industry directories, client case-study credits, podcasts, journalist quotes and genuine community answers. A 2026 study reported by Search Engine Land found Reddit, YouTube and LinkedIn among the sources AI search engines cite most.
Link your pages into clusters. Every guide should link to its service page and to two or three related guides with descriptive anchors.
Measure monthly and fix what is wrong. Track the reports below, and when an AI answer gets a fact about you wrong, correct the page it most likely came from first.

sections.heading: How to measure GEO without fooling yourself
paragraphs: Google Search Console now has a Generative AI performance report for supported features, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, with impressions by page, country, device and date. Bing Webmaster Tools has added an AI Performance report. These are the only first-party numbers available, so start there.

For ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini there is no full report. Keep a fixed panel of 10–20 buyer questions and check them on a set day each week or fortnight, logged out, recording the date, engine, exact question, whether you were cited, which URL, and which competitors appeared. Answers vary between runs, so treat the panel as a sample, not market share.

In GA4, look at referrals from chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, copilot.microsoft.com and gemini.google.com, and connect them to enquiries. Keep five numbers separate: mentions, AI impressions, visits, saved enquiries and qualified opportunities. An increase in mentions is not an increase in revenue until the later numbers move too.

sections.heading: GEO for Indian businesses: where the opportunity is
paragraphs: Many Indian categories have thin, generic content in English and almost none in Hindi, Gujarati or Bengali. AI answers can only cite what exists, so a manufacturer that publishes clear product applications, specifications, MOQ and dealer information often becomes the obvious source for its niche.

For D2C brands, the questions that matter are about suitability and comparison: which product for which use, sizing, care, delivery and returns. For service businesses and clinics, they are about cost ranges, process, eligibility and location. For each, the page that answers the question honestly and specifically is the page AI answers have a reason to use.

Local details matter too. Google says Merchant Center product data and Google Business Profiles can help products and businesses appear in AI responses, so keep both complete and consistent with your website.

sections.heading: What to ask a GEO agency before you hire one
paragraphs: Ask which engines and which questions are in scope, what the baseline is, how citations and referrals will be tracked, and what they will change on your site in the first 30 days. Ask how they will handle indexing and technical issues, because GEO built on unindexed pages produces nothing.

Be careful with anyone who guarantees citations in ChatGPT, sells a special AI schema or llms.txt as the main deliverable, or offers bulk mentions. At GrowwStack we run [AEO and GEO as part of our SEO services](/services#search-visibility), with the same measurement for both, and for selected partners we work with [no upfront fee and a share of the revenue the work produces](/partnership). Our [sports-equipment e-commerce case study](/case-studies/ecommerce-sports-equipment) reports online revenue from ₹0 to over ₹2.2 crore through organic growth with no paid ads; it is a reported outcome for that partner, not a promise for another business.

faq.q: What is generative engine optimization in simple words?
faq.a: Generative engine optimization (GEO) is making your website and business easy for AI answer tools such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT search and Perplexity to find, understand and cite, so they mention you correctly when someone asks a question you can answer.

Mostly no. AI answers retrieve pages from search indexes, so indexing, useful content and authority still decide most of the outcome. GEO adds a focus on entity consistency, third-party mentions and measuring AI visibility separately from ordinary rankings.

faq.q: What is the difference between GEO and AEO?
faq.a: AEO (answer engine optimization) usually means structuring content so it becomes the direct answer to a specific question. GEO usually means how your business is represented across AI-generated answers. The same accurate, well-structured page supports both. See the [AEO guide](/blog/answer-engine-optimization-aeo).

Google says it does not use llms.txt or other special AI files for Search, including its AI features. Some other tools may read the file, so it is harmless to keep one, but it is not a substitute for indexable pages and clear content.

faq.q: How long does GEO take to show results?
faq.a: It depends on whether your pages are already indexed and trusted. Fixing indexing and factual errors can change answers within weeks; earning citations for competitive questions usually takes months, because it depends on rankings and mentions on other sites.

faq.q: Can an agency guarantee that ChatGPT will recommend my business?
faq.a: No. AI answers vary between users and runs, and no outside party controls them. A credible agency promises a defined question panel, a baseline, specific page and authority work, and honest measurement, not a guaranteed recommendation.

takeaway: GEO is SEO with a sharper focus on being the clearest, most verifiable answer and the most consistently described business in your niche. Get indexed, answer real buyer questions with information only you have, earn genuine mentions, and measure AI visibility separately from enquiries.
